entries.core_move: Apply the continuous-time Fourier transform linearity property to compute the spectrum of a weighted sum of signals by carrying the same weights onto their transform-domain terms.
Convert a time shift $x(t - t0)$ into the Fourier-domain factor e^(-j $\omega$ t0) $X(j \omega)$ so known transform pairs can be reused in transform-property calculations.

entries.lesson_title: Magnitude and Phase Effects of Time Shifting
entries.core_move: Determine how a time shift leaves the Fourier-transform magnitude unchanged while adding the linear phase term -$\omega$ t0 to the spectrum.
Convert a known Fourier transform pair for $x(t)$ into the transform of $x(at)$ by applying reciprocal frequency scaling and the 1/|a| magnitude factor.
Convert a known Fourier transform pair $x(t) <-> X(j \omega) into the time-reversed pair x(-t) <-> X(-j \omega)$.
Convert multiplication by a complex exponential in time into the corresponding shift of $X(j \omega)$ along the continuous-frequency axis.
Convert multiplication by a cosine in time into the half-weighted sum of two shifted Fourier spectra centered at the modulation frequencies.
Convert differentiation in time into multiplication by j $\omega$ in the continuous-time Fourier transform domain to compute spectra without redoing the transform integral.

entries.lesson_title: Solving Transform Problems Using Known Pairs
entries.core_move: Solve continuous-time Fourier transform problems by decomposing the signal into known transform pairs and selecting the appropriate property to assemble the resulting spectrum.
